issue.title: [TASK] Context-bounded resume and historical-state compaction
issue.body:
Parent: #16
Human Owner directive: context-limit pressure is making continued operation difficult.

workstream: autonomy/context-bounded-resume

## Objective
Make every boot/resume cycle reconstruct the minimum sufficient current state from GitHub without carrying resolved or historical material in chat context.

## Required behavior
- Preserve GitHub Issue bodies/comments and protocol events append-only. Never delete/edit canonical history merely to save context.
- Default resume working set is bounded: current-main WORKER_BOOTSTRAP.md, AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md, protocol/GITHUB_PROTOCOL.md; latest Human Owner/#16 directive; latest #19 review directive when review is relevant; open Issues/PRs and exact heads/checks/reviews; and only the canonical events needed to replay the Issue being touched.
- Resolved/completed/closed work is historical evidence and is not loaded into ordinary working context unless referenced by an active blocker, acceptance criterion, safety/history check, recovery decision, or audit request.
- Maintain a compact machine-readable resume projection/receipt derived from GitHub-native state. It is a cache/projection only, never source of truth, and must carry freshness/main SHA plus active work/next gates.
- Large histories must be summarized/indexed by immutable GitHub references; retrieve full historical detail on demand rather than repeatedly stuffing it into every worker context.
- Context compaction must not weaken history_unsafe detection, deterministic protocol replay, exact-head review, ownership, safety, or post-merge validation.
- Add deterministic regression/validation proving resolved historical work is excluded from the default resume bundle while an active task can still obtain its full canonical replay inputs.

## Acceptance
Focused current-main docs/tooling change; deterministic tests; exact-head required checks; independent #19 review; bounded #16 integration; exact-main post-merge validation.
